title: A Cover for the Drop
premise: Silas Brightwater, a hostage negotiator haunted by the one call she couldn't save, is summoned when Flight 447's records vanish mid-flight — along with every passenger manifest, including her estranged brother. The disappearance is no accident: a private security firm called Meridian has built a technology that can erase people from reality's paperwork, and it was tested on that plane. As Silas infiltrates Meridian under the guise of negotiating with its founder, she discovers the firm trained her years ago and engineered her 'failure' as a loyalty test. To bring down the network and find her brother, she must decide whether to expose the truth and destroy the only people who ever believed in her — or accept power within it. In the end she burns Meridian from the inside, trading her own clean record for her brother's life and the truth.
about_author: Ansel Villalobos is a former crisis-line volunteer who spent six years listening to strangers talk each other back from ledges before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people who talk for a living, and lives in coastal Oregon with a deaf dog named Verdict.

chapters.title: The Call She Still Hears
chapters.summary: Silas Brightwater wakes at 3 a.m., as always, replaying the botched negotiation that killed a teenager two years ago. POV: Silas. Establishes her insomnia, her guilt, and her hollow routine at the bureau. Emotional beat: exhaustion masquerading as competence.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: A routine morning briefing shatters: Flight 447 is still airborne but no longer exists — no booking, no crew file, no radar history. Silas recognizes a passenger name on a scrap of recovered data: her brother Theo. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Silas and tech analyst Dev Okafor trace the erasure to a proprietary system too clean to be a glitch. Someone inside aviation administration is helping. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing the world's records can lie.

chapters.title: The Man Who Owns Nothing
chapters.summary: Silas interviews Aldous Vane, Meridian's founder, who owns no property, holds no title, and smiles like a man being patient. He offers her a consulting job. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the seduction of being seen by someone powerful.

chapters.title: What Meridian Trains
chapters.summary: Inside Meridian's campus, Silas finds negotiation simulators — and footage of herself, younger, in their training program she barely remembers applying to. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition; her past isn't hers alone.

chapters.title: Dev's Doubt
chapters.summary: Dev discovers Meridian funded the bureau's crisis protocol — meaning Silas's entire career was shaped by them. He begs her to walk away. POV: Dev. Emotional beat: friendship strained by protective fear.

chapters.title: The Incident, Replayed
chapters.summary: Meridian shows Silas sealed recordings of her failed negotiation, revealing a second voice fed into her earpiece that night — theirs. Her failure was manufactured. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief curdling into rage.

chapters.title: Landing Without a Plane
chapters.summary: A witness surfaces: a ground controller who saw Flight 447 land at a private strip, then watched the passengers escorted away alive. Theo may be alive. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: hope as a dangerous drug.

chapters.title: The Retention Program
chapters.summary: Silas learns of Meridian's 'retention' facility where erased people are held until they agree to disappear voluntarily — or are broken into assets. POV: alternating Silas/interrogation transcripts. Emotional beat: horror administered politely.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Vane admits everything over dinner: erasure is a service for governments and corporations, and he wants Silas to run its human side. He frames it as mercy — fewer bodies, cleaner exits. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: A whistleblower inside Meridian is found erased mid-sentence — his family no longer remembers him. Silas realizes cooperation doesn't buy safety, only delay. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the illusion of deal-making collapses.

chapters.title: Brother
chapters.summary: Silas reaches Theo by smuggled phone. He's alive but complicit — he took Meridian's money years ago and helped build the retention program. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: love complicated by betrayal on both sides.

chapters.title: Double Blind
chapters.summary: Silas agrees to Vane's offer while feeding evidence to Dev and an inspector general. Every conversation becomes a negotiation where both sides know they're lying. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the thrill and rot of double agency.

chapters.title: The Earpiece Again
chapters.summary: On her first assignment, Silas hears the second voice in her earpiece — guiding her to talk a target into self-erasure. She stalls, and the target dies anyway. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: her old failure repeating with new clarity.

chapters.title: Dev Burned
chapters.summary: Meridian identifies Dev as the leak. Silas must choose: expose herself to save him or let him be erased to protect the case. She chooses Dev, burning months of work. POV: Dev. Emotional beat: loyalty outranking the mission.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: Dev, hidden in Silas's apartment, decrypts Meridian's master archive: every erased person, including the true passenger list of Flight 447 — and orders signed not by Vane but by a bureau director. POV: Dev. Emotional beat: the conspiracy reaching home.

chapters.title: Negotiating With the Devil
chapters.summary: Silas confronts Director Hale, who offers her everything — Theo freed, record cleared, career restored — if the archive stays buried. It's the negotiation of her life, and this time she controls the room. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: power finally in her hands, and how it fits.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Hale moves first: Theo is transferred for permanent erasure at dawn. Silas realizes she's been played — her acceptance of Vane's job was always the test. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: cornered, sleepless, done being handled.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Silas leads a raid on the retention facility, using every trick Meridian taught her against them. Vane, unexpectedly, lets her through — he wanted the archive out; his empire had become something he didn't build. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: catharsis through competence.

chapters.title: What the Records Say
chapters.summary: The archive goes public. Hearings begin; Hale falls; thousands of erased names return to the world's paperwork. But some passengers chose to stay gone. POV: mixed, via news fragments and testimony. Emotional beat: truth as imperfect restitution.

chapters.title: Theo
chapters.summary: Silas and Theo meet in a courthouse hallway. He won't forgive her for exposing his crimes; she won't apologize for choosing truth. They part as adults, which is its own kind of repair. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief accepted rather than solved.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Months later, Silas negotiates one last hostage standoff — clean, unassisted, hers. That night she sleeps through till morning. The failure stays on the board, but so does she. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet survival as victory.
